io_rationale: A20; ubiquitin-editing brake on NF-kB. KO amplifies NF-kB-driven activation/effector output in T cells.

tractability.assessment: partially_tractable (OTU deubiquitinase enzymatic domain) but no approved/clinical drug; enzyme-restoration (agonism) is the harder therapeutic direction
tractability.evidence: ChEMBL target CHEMBL4523200; OTU DUB + A20 zinc fingers with PDB structures. No drug in ChEMBL mechanisms.

genetic_evidence.anchor_disease: SLE, rheumatoid arthritis, psoriasis, IBD, coeliac (canonical multi-autoimmune locus)
genetic_evidence.rationale: One of the best-established human autoimmune loci; reduced A20 function -> unrestrained NF-kB -> autoimmune RISK. LoF -> risk.
genetic_evidence.interpretation_note: Strong human proof that A20 is a bona fide immune brake; 'discordant' under a cancer-anchored rule but powerful mechanistic support.

known_drugs.note: No direct A20-targeted drug in clinic.

safety_flags: A20 is a tumor suppressor — biallelic LoF drives B-cell lymphomas (MALT/DLBCL). Permanent KO carries an oncogenic/autoimmune safety flag. STRONG de-prioritization for durable KO.
